thread:
alex: FYI — Velox (customer) on our Dedicated GPU pool seeing intermittent 403/connection reset when routing through their corporate proxy. They can reach other public APIs fine. Any checklist for outbound firewall/proxy requirements we can send them?

maria: Can you paste the failing curl + headers they used? Also which FQDN/IP are they hitting?

alex: They hit api-inference.redwood.com (443) via an outbound HTTP CONNECT proxy. Example they tried:

```\ncurl -v --proxy http://proxy.corp:8080 https://api-inference.redwood.com/v1/generate \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'\n```

Response: TLS handshake managed by curl but proxy returns 403 on CONNECT or closes the socket.

raj: Most common causes: proxy blocking CONNECT or TLS SNI being stripped/modified. Some corp proxies terminate TLS and re-sign which can break cert pinning or SNI-based routing on our CDN.

raj: Quick checklist to share with Velox:
- Allow outbound TCP to our service endpoints on port 443 (and 80 for health probes if they insist on TLS offload).
- Allow HTTP CONNECT method to the FQDNs (not just IPs) or permit transparent passthrough.
- Preserve TLS SNI and Host headers for CONNECT tunnels.
- Do NOT rewrite Host header for CONNECT tunnels.
- Allow long-lived connections for streaming endpoints (chunked/HTTP2).

maria: Can we give them an allowlist of IP ranges (CIDRs) they can add to their egress firewall? They'll prefer IPs. Note: our infra uses multiple cloud regions and CDNs, so ranges may change. 

raj: We can provide the current egress prefixes for the Dedicated region they use (ap-east-1 style example). Tell them these are the static NAT pools for that customer tenancy. Example (send as guidance, warn about rotation):

```
# Example allowlist (region:dedi-us-west-2) - verify with support before finalizing
54.152.128.0/18
35.77.128.0/17
18.194.0.0/15
15.188.0.0/16
# Ports: 443 (required), 80 (optional for health checks)
```

alex: They asked whether DNS-based allowlisting is safe. They tried allowing api-inference.redwood.com but their proxy resolves it to internal cache IPs and blocks others.

raj: DNS-only is risky because CDNs and NAT pools can rotate. If they can only accept DNS names, recommend allowing the FQDN and enabling outbound CONNECT passthrough. If they require IPs, add a monitoring/automation step to pull our published IP list and sync with their firewall daily.

maria: Any headers or proxy config we require? Some customers strip the Authorization header on proxy.

raj: Important proxy behaviour for us:
- Must forward Authorization header for CONNECT->tunnelled HTTPS (should be inside TLS, so proxy typically doesn't alter).
- Must not perform HTTP-level request-body rewrites for CONNECT tunnels.
- For non-CONNECT (if they use proxy with TLS termination), they need to allowlist our OCSP/CRL endpoints and accept our cert chain.

alex: Also callout for healthchecks / LB probes: if they have egress allowlist against our health endpoints (for Dedicated control plane) we provide a small set of service probe IPs. Those are separate from the general NAT pool. We gave them these before: 198.51.100.10 and 198.51.100.11 (example). Remind them these are for control-plane pings only.

raj: Streaming / websockets: require persistent TCP (80/443) and allow websocket upgrades. Some proxies close idle connections after 30s which breaks streaming. Ask them to increase idle timeout to >= 2m.

maria: Anything around TLS versions/ciphers? We had a recent case where proxy downgraded to TLS1.0 and broke ALPN/HTTP2 -> streaming failure.

raj: Minimum TLS 1.2, prefer 1.3. ALPN for h2 should be allowed. If they do TLS inspection, our cert pinning might fail; in that case you need to either: 1) allow passthrough for our domain, or 2) add our CA to their intercepting proxy trust store and allow SNI mapping.

alex: I'll send Velox the checklist + the example CIDRs with the strong warning about rotation and to open a support ticket for a definitive list for their Dedicated tenancy.

sre-oncall-bot: NOTE: If customer requests static egress IP guarantees for Dedicated, escalate to eng-infra + account team. There may be a small-networking change window (2-5 business days).

maria: Action items:
- raj: produce a short one-pager (2-3 bullets + example firewall rules + curl snippet) we can email to customers.
- alex: open support ticket for Velox to get their Dedicated-tenant static NAT pool list and expected rotation cadence.

raj: I'll draft the one-pager and include this sample firewall snippet customers can paste into common proxies/firewalls:

```
# Palo Alto / Fortigate style example
set firewall policy allow-redwood-outbound
  source-zone internal
  destination-zone internet
  destination-address [54.152.128.0/18,35.77.128.0/17,18.194.0.0/15,15.188.0.0/16]
  service TCP/443 allow
  application any
  action allow
  enable http-connect-method
  description "Allow outbound to Redwood Dedicated inference endpoints"
```

alex: perfect. small note: add a reminder to run a connectivity test: `curl --proxy http://<proxy>:8080 -I https://api-inference.redwood.com/health` and capture the raw CONNECT response.

maria: LGTM. raj -> assign to you to share final doc in #customer-success once done. :thumbsup:

alex: Thanks team. I'll follow up with Velox and paste updates here. :white_check_mark:
